key_insight: Al-Zn grain boundary diffusion, especially at 900°C, significantly boosts NdFeB coercivity by improving grain-boundary decoupling and forming a beneficial core-shell microstructure.
engineering_relevance: This offers a non-heavy-rare-earth route to make sintered NdFeB magnets more thermally robust for high-temperature motor and actuator applications.
method: Applied Al80Zn20 alloy sheets at both ends of cylindrical NdFeB samples
Diffusion-annealed at 900°C or 700°C for 7 h under high vacuum, then tempered at 500°C for 2 h
Characterized magnetism and microstructure using magnetic testing, SEM/EDS, and XRD
evidence_signal: Coercivity increased from 951.5 kA/m to 1158.2 kA/m at 900°C, while remanence decreased only modestly from 1282 mT to 1256 mT.
watch_item: The improved performance depends on tightly controlled high-temperature vacuum diffusion, and the higher-temperature treatment may require careful management to avoid remanence loss or process variability.
paper_title: Effect of Al-Zn alloy wafer grain boundary diffusion on the magnetism and microstructure of sintered NdFeB magnets
